title: Two words in the Preamble weren't there in 1949
sources: Preamble to the Constitution of India (text incl. 'this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949')
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973); Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India, Supreme Court, 25 November 2024

quiz.q: On which date was the Constitution adopted?
quiz.why: Right. The Preamble records adoption on 26 November 1949; most of the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

script: The Preamble opens with: We, the people of India.
It calls India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.
But socialist and secular weren't in the text adopted on 26 November 1949.
But socialist and secular weren't in the text adopted on the twenty-sixth of November, nineteen forty-nine.
The forty-second Amendment added them in nineteen seventy-six.
In Kesavananda Bharati, in nineteen seventy-three,
the Supreme Court treated the Preamble as part of the Constitution.
In November 2024, it dismissed challenges to the 1976 words:
In November twenty twenty-four, it dismissed challenges to the nineteen seventy-six words:
the amending power extends to the Preamble.
On which date was the Constitution adopted?

claims.claim: The Preamble begins 'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA' and describes a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC, with JUSTICE, LIBERTY, EQUALITY and FRATERNITY
The Preamble records adoption 'this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949' (26 November 1949)
The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted 'socialist' and 'secular' into the Preamble
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) established that the Preamble is part of the Constitution

On 25 November 2024 the Supreme Court (CJI Khanna, Justice Sanjay Kumar) dismissed petitions challenging the 1976 insertion, holding the amending power under Article 368 extends to the Preamble (2024)

review_note: Preamble text read from an institutional PDF and an explainer, not the Gazette copy. 'The authority starts with us' is an editorial gloss on 'We, the people'. Left out: 'unity and integrity' wording change in 1976 (not confirmed by two sources here), Berubari (1960), the Emergency context. 26 January 1950 as commencement is in the quiz explanation only; check before release.
